title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 36th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. Where a party requests confirmation that the arbitration agreement does not exist on the ground that the arbitration clause has not been formed, the people's court shall review the request as an application for confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement.

2. An arbitration clause exists independently. Its formation and validity are independent and severable from other clauses of the contract. If the parties negotiated the arbitration clause at the time of concluding the contract and reached an agreement to submit to arbitration, whether the contract is formed or not does not affect the formation and validity of the arbitration clause.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuance of the 36th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2022] No. 267

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and approval by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following six cases (Guiding Cases No. 196-201), including the case of Yunyu Limited v. Shenzhen Zhongyuancheng Commercial Investment Holding Co., Ltd. — application for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement, are hereby issued as the 36th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

December 27, 2022

Guiding Case No. 196

Yunyu Limited v. Shenzhen Zhongyuancheng Commercial Investment Holding Co., Ltd. — application for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement

(Deliberated and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court and issued on December 27, 2022)

Keywords: civil; application for confirmation of validity of arbitration agreement; formation of arbitration clause

Ruling Gist

1. Where a party requests a confirmation that no arbitration agreement exists on the ground that the arbitration clause was not formed, the people's court shall review the case as one for application for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement.

2. An arbitration clause exists independently; its formation and validity are separate and severable from other terms of the contract. Where the parties have negotiated the arbitration clause during the formation of the contract and have reached a consensus on submitting to arbitration, the formation or non-formation of the contract does not affect the formation or validity of the arbitration clause.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 16, Article 19, and Paragraph 1 of Article 20 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

China Tourism Group Corporation Limited (hereinafter referred to as "China Tourism Group"), formerly named China Tourism Group Corporation and China Travel Service (Hong Kong) Group Limited, is a wholly state-owned company. Hong Kong China Travel Service (Group) Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as "Hong Kong China Travel Service") is a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Tourism Group, registered in Hong Kong. Yunyu Limited (hereinafter referred to as "Yunyu Company") is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hong Kong China Travel Service, registered in the British Virgin Islands. Xinjin Company is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Yunyu Company, also registered in the British Virgin Islands.

On March 24, 2016, China Tourism Group issued the "Approval on Consent to the Listing and Transfer of 100% Equity of NEWPOWER ENTERPRISES INC.", approving Yunyu Company to lawfully and compliantly transfer its 100% equity in Xinjin Company. On March 29, 2017, Yunyu Company publicly listed and transferred its 100% equity in Xinjin Company through the Beijing Equity Exchange. Shenzhen Zhongyuancheng Commercial Investment Holding Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Zhongyuancheng Company"), as an intended transferee, engaged in negotiations with Yunyu Company and other parties regarding the execution of the property rights transaction contract for the project in question.

On May 9, 2017, Zhang Xin, Manager of the Investment Management Department of Hong Kong CTS Hotels Company Limited (a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Tourism Group), sent an email to Zhang Ruirui, Risk Control and Legal Affairs Officer of Shenzhen Tailong Financial Holding Group Co., Ltd. (the parent group company of Zhongyuancheng Company). The attachment to the email, the "Property Rights Transaction Contract," was a standard form provided by the Beijing Equity Exchange, stating that Party A was Yunyu Company, Party B was Zhongyuancheng Company, and the parties executed the contract for the transfer of Yunyu Company's 100% equity in Xinjin Company to Zhongyuancheng Company in accordance with the Contract Law, the Interim Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises, and other relevant laws, regulations, and rules. Article 16 of the contract, titled "Jurisdiction and Dispute Resolution Method," provided: "16.1 This contract and the acts in the property rights transaction shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China; 16.2 Any dispute between the parties arising from the interpretation or performance of this contract shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration." Article 12 of the attached "Debt Settlement Agreement" in the same email provided: "This agreement is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. Any dispute between the parties arising from the interpretation or performance of this agreement shall be resolved through negotiation among the parties; if negotiation fails, any party has the right to submit the dispute to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration."

On May 10, 2017, Zhang Ruirui sent an email to Zhang Xin and Liu Zhen, stating: "Attached is our company's proposed amendments to the contract. Please give them due consideration on the principles of equality, fairness, and effectiveness of the contract upon signing." In the attachments to this email, Article 16 of the "Property Rights Transaction Contract" text was amended to: "16.1 This contract and the acts in the property rights transaction shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China; 16.2 Any dispute between the parties arising from the interpretation or performance of this contract shall be resolved through negotiation; if negotiation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court for arbitration." Article 12 of the "Debt Settlement Agreement" text was amended to: "This agreement is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. Any dispute between the parties arising from the interpretation or performance of this agreement shall be resolved through negotiation among the parties; if negotiation fails, any party has the right to submit the dispute to the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court for arbitration."

On May 11, 2017, at 1:42 p.m., Zhang Xin sent an email to Zhang Ruirui and Li Jun, a senior officer of Zhongyuancheng Company, responding to Zhongyuancheng Company's proposed amendments to the two contract texts, and stating: "We are sending you the revised draft contract for signing. Please provide your feedback as soon as possible after receiving the attached content. The contract confirmed by you and our company will be submitted to the Beijing Equity Exchange and our company's internal approval process, and may only be signed after final confirmation by the Beijing Equity Exchange and our group company (if there are further modifications, we will confirm with you again)." Article 16 of the "Property Rights Transaction Contract (Draft for Signing)" attached to this email and Article 12 of the "Debt Settlement Agreement (Draft for Signing)" were identical to the corresponding provisions in the attachments to the email sent by Zhang Ruirui to Zhang Xin and Liu Zhen on May 10. On the same day at 6:39 p.m., Zhang Ruirui sent an email to Zhang Xin, stating: "Attached are the scanned copies of the signed 'Property Rights Transaction Contract (Draft for Signing)' and 'Debt Settlement Agreement (Draft for Signing)', as well as the project signing explanation letter, etc. Please check and reply." The provisions on jurisdiction and dispute resolution in the attached "Property Rights Transaction Contract (Draft for Signing)" and "Debt Settlement Agreement (Draft for Signing)" were the same as those in the attachments to the email sent by Zhang Xin on the same day. Zhongyuancheng Company affixed its seal to the contracts and delivered the texts to Yunyu Company.

On May 17, 2017, Zhang Xin sent an email to Li Jun, stating: "The final approval process of our group company for the Shenzhen project is currently underway. If the approval goes smoothly, we plan to hold the signing ceremony on the morning of this Friday at the Beijing View Metropolitan Hotel. We will inform you of the specific circumstances after confirmation from our company. We are sending you the proposed signing versions of the 'Property Rights Transaction Contract' and 'Debt Settlement Agreement' in advance for your review." Attachment 1 to this email was the "Property Rights Transaction Contract for Equity Transfer Project (Proposed Signing Version)", and Attachment 2 was the "Debt Settlement Agreement for Equity Transfer Project (Proposed Signing Version)". The arbitration clauses in these two contract texts remained the same as those in the draft for signing.

On October 27, 2017, Yunyu Company sent a letter to Zhongyuancheng Company canceling the transaction. On April 4, 2018, Zhongyuancheng Company filed an arbitration application with the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court pursuant to Article 16.2 of the "Property Rights Transaction Contract (Draft for Signing)" and Article 12 of the "Debt Settlement Agreement (Draft for Signing)", naming Yunyu Company and others as co-respondents. Before the arbitral tribunal held a hearing, Yunyu Company and others filed separate lawsuits with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, applying for confirmation that no arbitration agreement existed. The court accepted the cases on September 11, 2018, resulting in this case and two related cases. During the review by the Intermediate People's Court, the Supreme People's Court considered that this case and the related cases were of significant legal importance, and that review by the International Commercial Court would facilitate the uniform application of law and improve the efficiency of dispute resolution. Therefore, pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law and Item 5 of Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Establishment of International Commercial Courts, the Supreme People's Court ordered that this case be reviewed by the First International Commercial Court of the Supreme People's Court.

Judgment

The Supreme People's Court, on September 18, 2019, rendered the Civil Ruling (2019) Zui Gao Fa Min Te No. 1, rejecting the application of Yunyu Limited.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held: After Zhongyuancheng Company applied for arbitration, Yunyu Company, on the ground that the arbitration clause was not formed, applied to the people's court for a confirmation that no valid arbitration clause existed between the parties. Although this differs from a request for confirmation that an arbitration agreement is invalid, whether an arbitration agreement exists or is valid directly affects the method of dispute resolution, and both are preliminary issues that need to be resolved. Therefore, a request for confirmation that no arbitration agreement exists between the parties also falls within the broad scope of objections to the validity of an arbitration agreement. Paragraph 1 of Article 20 of the Arbitration Law provides: "If a party challenges the validity of the arbitration agreement, it may request the arbitration commission to make a decision or request the people's court to make a ruling." Accordingly, a party requesting confirmation that an arbitration agreement does not exist on the ground that the arbitration clause was not formed is a case for application for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement, and the people's court shall accept and review the case.

When confirming the validity of an arbitration agreement, the applicable law must first be determined. Article 18 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations provides: "The parties may agree on the law applicable to the arbitration agreement. If the parties have not so chosen, the law of the place of the arbitration institution or the law of the place of arbitration shall apply." During the court's inquiry, all parties expressly agreed to apply the laws of the People's Republic of China to determine the validity of the arbitration agreement at issue. Therefore, the arbitration agreement in this case is governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China.

Paragraph 1 of Article 16 of the Arbitration Law provides: "An arbitration agreement includes an arbitration clause contained in a contract and any other written agreement for arbitration reached before or after the dispute arises." It can be seen that both types—an arbitration clause in a contract and a separate arbitration agreement—constitute arbitration agreements, and the formation and validity of an arbitration clause are subject to the same legal provisions governing arbitration agreements.

The independence of an arbitration agreement is a widely recognized fundamental legal principle, meaning that an arbitration agreement is severable from the main contract, and they are independent from each other; their existence, validity, and the applicable law are all severable. Since an arbitration clause is the main type of arbitration agreement and appears in the same document as other contract terms, giving independence to an arbitration clause is of greater practical significance than emphasizing the independence of a separate arbitration agreement. It can even be said that the independence of an arbitration agreement primarily refers to the severability of the arbitration clause from the main contract. Both the laws of the People's Republic of China and judicial interpretations provide for the independence of an arbitration agreement. Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Arbitration Law provides: "An arbitration agreement shall exist independently, and the amendment, rescission, termination, or invalidity of the contract shall not affect the validity of the arbitration agreement." In context, this provision, following Article 16 of the Arbitration Law which clarifies that an arbitration clause constitutes an arbitration agreement, provides for the independence of the arbitration agreement. Therefore, an arbitration clause is independent of the contract. However, the provisions of the Arbitration Law on whether an arbitration clause can be formed completely independently of the contract are not particularly clear, unlike the explicit provision that the amendment, rescission, termination, or invalidity of an already formed contract does not affect the validity of the arbitration agreement. In judicial practice, the issues of whether a contract is formed and whether its arbitration clause is formed are often intertwined. However, the opening phrase of Paragraph 1 of Article 19 of the Arbitration Law, "An arbitration agreement shall exist independently," is a general and overarching statement that should cover the issue of whether an arbitration agreement exists, i.e., whether it is formed. The subsequent statements further emphasize that even the enumerated types of situations cannot affect the validity of the arbitration agreement. Paragraph 2 of Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China further clarifies: "If the parties reach an arbitration agreement on the dispute when concluding the contract, the non-formation of the contract shall not affect the validity of the arbitration agreement." Therefore, when determining the validity of an arbitration clause, including whether it is formed, the validity of the arbitration clause itself may be determined first; only when it is truly necessary should the validity of the entire contract, including whether the contract is formed, be considered. This case also follows this rule, first determining whether the arbitration clause was formed based on the specific circumstances of this case.

The issue of whether an arbitration clause is formed primarily concerns whether the parties have reached a consensus to submit the dispute to arbitration, i.e., whether an arbitration agreement has been reached. An arbitration agreement is a contract. Whether the parties have reached a consensus on arbitration should be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Contract Law on offer and acceptance. Judging from the negotiation circumstances of this case, the parties had consistently agreed to submit the dispute to arbitration. The earliest "Property Rights Transaction Contract" in this case was a standard form provided by the Beijing Equity Exchange, which, together with the "Debt Settlement Agreement," was sent by Yunyu Company and others to Zhongyuancheng Company. Both contracts contained clauses for submitting disputes to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration. Subsequently, the parties negotiated on the arbitration institution. The arbitration clause in the draft for signing sent by Yunyu Company and others had designated the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court as the arbitration institution. As far as the arbitration clause was concerned, this constituted an offer made by Yunyu Company and others. Zhongyuancheng Company affixed its seal to the draft for signing, indicating acceptance, and delivered the sealed contract text to Yunyu Company on May 11, 2017. This constituted Zhongyuancheng Company's acceptance. According to Articles 25 and 26 of the Contract Law, an acceptance becomes effective when the notice of acceptance reaches the offeror, and a contract is formed when the acceptance becomes effective. Therefore, the arbitration clauses in the "Property Rights Transaction Contract" and the "Debt Settlement Agreement" were formed between the respective parties on May 11, 2017. Thereafter, the parties negotiated on certain other matters of the contracts but never disputed the arbitration clauses. Since Yunyu Company and others did not assert that the arbitration clause suffered from statutory grounds for invalidity, it should be determined that a valid arbitration clause exists between the parties, and the dispute between them should be arbitrated by the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court. Although Yunyu Company and others did not affix their seal to the final contract text, nor did their legal representatives sign the text, which did not comply with the requirement that the contract take effect upon being signed and sealed by the legal representatives or authorized representatives of both parties, according to Paragraph 2 of Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China, even if the contract is not formed, the validity of the arbitration clause is not affected. Where the parties have already reached an arbitration agreement, it is unnecessary to further determine whether the contract in this case is formed; that issue should be resolved in the arbitration. In summary, the reasons and requests of Yunyu Company cannot be established, and the people's court rejected its application.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhang Yongjian, Gao Xiaoli, Xi Xiangyang, Ding Guangyu, Shen Hongyu)

Guiding Case No. 197

Shenzhen Shizheng Gongying Investment Holding Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Transportation — application for confirmation of validity of arbitration agreement

(Deliberated and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court and issued on December 27, 2022)

Keywords: civil; application for confirmation of validity of arbitration agreement; first hearing; re-arbitration

Ruling Gist

If a party fails to raise an objection to the validity of an arbitration agreement before the first hearing before the arbitral tribunal, it shall be deemed that the party has accepted the jurisdiction of the arbitral tribunal over the case. Although the case may re-enter the arbitration proceedings, it is still an arbitration proceeding for the same dispute. Where a party raises an objection to the validity of the arbitration agreement before the hearing in the re-arbitration, it does not fall within the circumstance of "raising before the first hearing before the arbitral tribunal" as provided in Paragraph 2 of Article 20 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Paragraph 2 of Article 20 of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

Shenzhen Shizheng Gongying Investment Holding Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Shizheng Gongying Company") alleged: The dispute between Shizheng Gongying Company and the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Transportation was decided by the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court on February 20, 2020, to re-arbitrate. The case has not yet been reconstituted and is at a stage before the first hearing. The two case proceedings are independent of each other. Therefore, the time for filing the application for confirmation of the validity of the arbitration agreement should be deemed to be before the first hearing. The first-instance ruling's application of Article 13 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China constitutes an error in the application of law.

The Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Transportation, Guangdong Province, argued in defense: The arbitration case in question had its first hearing on August 18, 2017. During the hearing, Shizheng Gongying Company confirmed on the record that it had no objection to the proceedings already conducted by the arbitral tribunal. Shizheng Gongying Company had already recognized the jurisdiction of the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court over the arbitration case. It cannot reacquire the right it had waived simply because the case entered re-arbitration proceedings. The first-instance ruling applied the law correctly.

The court found upon trial: The South China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (also known as the Shenzhen International Arbitration Court, formerly known as the South China Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission and the Shenzhen Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission) accepted the arbitration case in question in 2016. On August 18, 2017, the arbitral tribunal held a hearing. Before the arbitration applicant stated and finalized the facts and grounds for its arbitration requests, the tribunal asked: "Do the parties have any objections to the proceedings already conducted in this case?" The applicant in this case answered: "No objection." At the conclusion of the hearing, the applicant in this case stated that it had "no objection to the arbitration proceedings conducted up to this point." On March 29, 2018, the South China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission rendered an arbitral award. After the award was rendered, Shizheng Gongying Company applied to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court for non-enforcement of the arbitral award. Upon review, the court considered that the arbitral tribunal could re-arbitrate, and since the arbitral tribunal had agreed to re-arbitrate within the time limit specified by the court, the review procedure for non-enforcement of the arbitral award should be terminated. On February 26, 2020, the court rendered a ruling terminating the review procedure in that case.

Judgment

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, on June 3, 2020, rendered the Civil Ruling (2020) Yue 03 Min Te No. 249, rejecting the application of the applicant Shizheng Gongying Company. Shizheng Gongying Company appealed, and the Guangdong High People's Court, on September 18, 2020, rendered the Civil Ruling (2020) Yue Min Zhong No. 2212, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original ruling.

Reasoning

法院生效裁判认为：《中华人民共和国仲裁法》第二十条第二款规定：“当事人对仲裁协议的效力有异议，应当在仲裁庭首次开庭前提出”，当事人未在仲裁庭首次开庭前对仲裁协议的效力提出异议的，视为当事人接受仲裁庭对案件的管辖权。本案虽然进入重新仲裁程序，但仍为同一纠纷，实正共盈公司在仲裁过程中未对仲裁协议效力提出异议并确认对仲裁程序无异议，其行为在重新仲裁过程中仍具有效力。根据《最高人民法院关于适用〈中华人民共和国仲裁法〉若干问题的解释》第十三条“依照仲裁法第二十条第二款的规定，当事人在仲裁庭首次开庭前没有对仲裁协议的效力提出异议，而后向人民法院申请确认仲裁协议无效的，人民法院不予受理”的规定，一审法院不应受理实正共盈公司提出的确认仲裁协议效力申请。一审法院受理本案后，根据《最高人民法院审理仲裁司法审查案件若干问题的规定》第八条第一款“人民法院立案后发现不符合受理条件的，裁定驳回申请”的规定，裁定驳回实正共盈公司的申请，并无不当。

（生效裁判审判人员：辜恩臻、潘晓璇、贺伟）

指导性案例198号

中国工商银行股份有限公司岳阳分行与刘友良申请撤销仲裁裁决案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过 2022年12月27日发布）

关键词 民事/申请撤销仲裁裁决/仲裁协议/实际施工人

裁判要点

实际施工人并非发包人与承包人签订的施工合同的当事人，亦未与发包人、承包人订立有效仲裁协议，不应受发包人与承包人的仲裁协议约束。实际施工人依据发包人与承包人的仲裁协议申请仲裁，仲裁机构作出仲裁裁决后，发包人请求撤销仲裁裁决的，人民法院应予支持。

相关法条

《中华人民共和国仲裁法》第58条

基本案情

2012年8月30日，中国工商银行股份有限公司岳阳分行（以下简称工行岳阳分行）与湖南巴陵建设有限公司（以下简称巴陵公司）签订《装修工程施工合同》，工行岳阳分行将其办公大楼整体装修改造内部装饰项目发包给巴陵公司，同时在合同第15.11条约定“本合同发生争议时，先由双方协商解决，协商不成时，向岳阳仲裁委员会申请仲裁解决。”2012年9月10日，巴陵公司与刘友良签订《内部项目责任承包合同书》，巴陵公司将工行岳阳分行办公大楼整体装修改造内部装饰项目的工程内容及保修以大包干方式承包给刘友良，并收取一定的管理费及相关保证金。2013年7月23日，工行岳阳分行与巴陵公司又签订了《装饰安装工程施工补充合同》，工行岳阳分行将其八楼主机房碳纤维加固、防水、基层装饰、外屏管道整修、室内拆旧及未进入决算的相关工程发包给巴陵公司。由于工行岳阳分行未能按照约定支付工程款，2017年7月4日，刘友良以工行岳阳分行为被申请人向岳阳仲裁委员会申请仲裁。2017年8月7日，工行岳阳分行以其与刘友良未达成仲裁协议为由提出仲裁管辖异议。2017年8月8日，岳阳仲裁委员会以岳仲决字〔2017〕8号决定驳回了工行岳阳分行的仲裁管辖异议。2017年12月22日，岳阳仲裁委员会作出岳仲决字〔2017〕696号裁决，裁定工行岳阳分行向刘友良支付到期应付工程价款及违约金。工行岳阳分行遂向湖南省岳阳市中级人民法院申请撤销该仲裁裁决。

裁判结果

湖南省岳阳市中级人民法院于2018年11月12日作出（2018）湘06民特1号民事裁定，撤销岳阳仲裁委员会岳仲决字〔2017〕696号裁决。

裁判理由

法院生效裁判认为，仲裁协议是当事人达成的自愿将他们之间业已产生或可能产生的有关特定的无论是契约性还是非契约性的法律争议的全部或特定争议提交仲裁的合意。仲裁协议是仲裁机构取得管辖权的依据，是仲裁合法性、正当性的基础，其集中体现了仲裁自愿原则和协议仲裁制度。本案中，工行岳阳分行与巴陵公司签订的《装修工程施工合同》第15.11条约定“本合同发生争议时，先由双方协商解决，协商不成时，向岳阳仲裁委员会申请仲裁”，故工行岳阳分行与巴陵公司之间因工程款结算及支付引起的争议应当通过仲裁解决。但刘友良作为实际施工人，其并非工行岳阳分行与巴陵公司签订的《装修工程施工合同》的当事人，刘友良与工行岳阳分行及巴陵公司之间均未达成仲裁合意，不受该合同中仲裁条款的约束。除非另有约定，刘友良无权援引工行岳阳分行与巴陵公司之间《装修工程施工合同》中的仲裁条款向合同当事方主张权利。刘友良以巴陵公司的名义施工，巴陵公司作为《装修工程施工合同》的主体仍然存在并承担相应的权利义务，案件当事人之间并未构成《最高人民法院关于适用〈中华人民共和国仲裁法〉若干问题的解释》第八条规定的合同仲裁条款“承继”情形，亦不构成上述解释第九条规定的合同主体变更情形。2004年《最高人民法院关于审理建设工程施工合同纠纷案件适用法律问题的解释》第二十六条虽然规定实际施工人可以发包人为被告主张权利且发包人只在欠付工程款的范围内对实际施工人承担责任，但上述内容仅规定了实际施工人对发包人的诉权以及发包人承担责任的范围，不应视为实际施工人援引《装修工程施工合同》中仲裁条款的依据。综上，工行岳阳分行与刘友良之间不存在仲裁协议，岳阳仲裁委员会基于刘友良的申请以仲裁方式解决工行岳阳分行与刘友良之间的工程款争议无法律依据。实际施工人依据发包人与承包人的仲裁协议申请仲裁，仲裁机构作出仲裁裁决后，发包人请求撤销仲裁裁决的，人民法院应予支持。

（生效裁判审判人员：闾开海、宋红燕、苏洁）

指导性案例199号

高哲宇与深圳市云丝路创新发展基金企业、李斌申请撤销仲裁裁决案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过 2022年12月27日发布）

关键词 民事/申请撤销仲裁裁决/比特币/社会公共利益

裁判要点

仲裁裁决裁定被申请人赔偿与比特币等值的美元，再将美元折算成人民币，属于变相支持比特币与法定货币之间的兑付交易，违反了国家对虚拟货币金融监管的规定，违背了社会公共利益，人民法院应当裁定撤销仲裁裁决。

相关法条

《中华人民共和国仲裁法》第58条

基本案情

2017年12月2日，深圳市云丝路创新发展基金企业（以下简称云丝路企业）、高哲宇、李斌签订了《股权转让协议》，根据该协议约定，云丝路企业将其持有的深圳极驱科技有限公司（以下简称极驱公司）5%股权以55万元转让给高哲宇；李斌同意代替高哲宇向云丝路企业支付30万元股权转让款，高哲宇直接向云丝路企业支付25万元股权转让款，同时高哲宇将李斌委托其进行理财的比特币全部归还至李斌的电子钱包。该协议签订后，高哲宇未履行合同义务。

云丝路企业、李斌向深圳仲裁委员会申请仲裁，主要请求为：变更云丝路企业持有的极驱公司5%股权到高哲宇名下，高哲宇向云丝路企业支付股权款25万元，高哲宇向李斌归还与比特币资产相等价值的美金493158.40美元及利息，高哲宇支付李斌违约金10万元。

仲裁庭经审理认为，高哲宇未依照案涉合同的约定交付双方共同约定并视为有财产意义的比特币等，构成违约，应予赔偿。仲裁庭参考李斌提供的okcoin.com网站公布的合同约定履行时点有关比特币收盘价的公开信息，估算应赔偿的财产损失为401780美元。仲裁庭裁决，变更云丝路企业持有的极驱公司5%股权至高哲宇名下；高哲宇向云丝路企业支付股权转让款25万元；高哲宇向李斌支付401780美元（按裁决作出之日的美元兑人民币汇率结算为人民币）；高哲宇向李斌支付违约金10万元。

高哲宇认为该仲裁裁决违背社会公共利益，请求人民法院予以撤销。

裁判结果

广东省深圳市中级人民法院于2020年4月26日作出（2018）粤03民特719号民事裁定，撤销深圳仲裁委员会（2018）深仲裁字第64号仲裁裁决。

裁判理由

法院生效裁判认为：《中国人民银行 工业和信息化部 中国银行业监督管理委员会 中国证券监督管理委员会 中国保险监督管理委员会关于防范比特币风险的通知》（银发〔2013〕289号）明确规定，比特币不具有与货币等同的法律地位，不能且不应作为货币在市场上流通使用。2017年中国人民银行等七部委联合发布关于防范代币发行融资风险的公告，重申了上述规定，同时从防范金融风险的角度，进一步提出任何所谓的代币融资交易平台不得从事法定货币与代币、虚拟货币相互之间的兑换业务，不得买卖或作为中央对手方买卖代币或虚拟货币，不得为代币或虚拟货币提供定价、信息中介等服务。上述文件实质上禁止了比特币的兑付、交易及流通，炒作比特币等行为涉嫌从事非法金融活动，扰乱金融秩序，影响金融稳定。涉案仲裁裁决高哲宇赔偿李斌与比特币等值的美元，再将美元折算成人民币，实质上是变相支持了比特币与法定货币之间的兑付、交易，与上述文件精神不符，违背了社会公共利益，该仲裁裁决应予撤销。

（生效裁判审判人员：朱萍、梁乐乐、赵雪琳）

指导性案例200号

斯万斯克蜂蜜加工公司申请承认和执行外国仲裁裁决案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过 2022年12月27日发布）

关键词 民事/申请承认和执行外国仲裁裁决/快速仲裁/临时仲裁

裁判要点

仲裁协议仅约定通过快速仲裁解决争议，未明确约定仲裁机构的，由临时仲裁庭作出裁决，不属于《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》第五条第一款规定的情形，被申请人以采用临时仲裁不符合仲裁协议约定为由，主张不予承认和执行该临时仲裁裁决的，人民法院不予支持。

相关法条

1.《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第290条（本案适用的是2017年6月27日修正的《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第283条）

2.《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》第5条

基本案情

2013年5月17日，卖方南京常力蜂业有限公司（以下简称常力蜂业公司）与买方斯万斯克蜂蜜加工公司（Svensk Honungsförädling AB）（以下简称斯万斯克公司）签订了编号为NJRS13001的英文版蜂蜜销售《合同》，约定的争议解决条款为“in case of disputes governed by Swedish law and that disputes should be settled by Expedited Arbitration in Sweden.”（中文直译为：“在受瑞典法律管辖的情况下，争议应在瑞典通过快速仲裁解决。”）。另《合同》约定了相应的质量标准：蜂蜜其他参数符合欧洲（2001/112/EC，2001年12月20日），无美国污仔病、微粒子虫、瓦螨病等。

在合同履行过程中，双方因蜂蜜品质问题发生纠纷。2015年2月23日，斯万斯克公司以常力蜂业公司为被申请人就案涉《合同》向瑞典斯德哥尔摩商会仲裁院申请仲裁，请求常力蜂业公司赔偿。该仲裁院于2015年12月18日以其无管辖权为由作出SCCF2015/023仲裁裁决，驳回了斯万斯克公司的申请。

2016年3月22日，斯万斯克公司再次以常力蜂业公司为被申请人就案涉《合同》在瑞典申请临时仲裁。在仲裁审查期间，临时仲裁庭及斯德哥尔摩地方法院向常力蜂业公司及该公司法定代表人邮寄了相应材料，但截止2017年5月4日，临时仲裁庭除了收到常力蜂业公司关于陈述《合同》没有约定仲裁条款、不应适用瑞典法的两份电子邮件外，未收到其他任何意见。此后临时仲裁庭收到常力蜂业公司代理律师提交的关于反对仲裁庭管辖权及延长提交答辩书的意见书。2018年3月5日、6日，临时仲裁庭组织双方当事人进行了听证。听证中，常力蜂业公司的代理人对仲裁庭的管辖权不再持异议，常力蜂业公司的法定代表人赵上生也未提出相应异议。该临时仲裁庭于2018年6月9日依据瑞典仲裁法作出仲裁裁决：1.常力蜂业公司违反了《合同》约定，应向斯万斯克公司支付286 230美元及相应利息；2.常力蜂业公司应向斯万斯克公司赔偿781614瑞典克朗、1021718.45港元。

2018年11月22日，斯万斯克公司向江苏省南京市中级人民法院申请承认和执行上述仲裁裁决。

法院审查期间，双方均认为应当按照瑞典法律来理解《合同》中的仲裁条款。斯万斯克公司认为争议解决条款的中文意思是“如发生任何争议，应适用瑞典法律并在瑞典通过快速仲裁解决。”而常力蜂业公司则认为上述条款的中文意思是“为瑞典法律管辖下的争议在瑞典进行快速仲裁解决。”

裁判结果

江苏省南京市中级人民法院于2019年7月15日作出（2018）苏01协外认8号民事裁定，承认和执行由Peter Thorp、Sture Larsson和Nils Eliasson组成的临时仲裁庭于2018年6月9日针对斯万斯克公司与常力蜂业公司关于NJRS13001《合同》作出的仲裁裁决。

裁判理由

法院生效裁判认为：依据查明及认定的事实，由Peter Thorp、Sture Larsson和Nils Eliasson组成的临时仲裁庭作出的案涉仲裁裁决不具有《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》第五条第一款乙、丙、丁项规定的不予承认和执行的情形，也不违反我国加入该公约时所作出的保留性声明条款，或违反我国公共政策或争议事项不能以仲裁解决的情形，故对该裁决应当予以承认和执行。

关于临时仲裁裁决的程序是否存在与仲裁协议不符的情形。该项争议系双方对《合同》约定的争议解决条款“in case of disputes governed by Swedish law and that disputes should be settled by Expedited Arbitration in Sweden.”的理解问题。从双方对该条款中文意思的表述看，双方对在瑞典通过快速仲裁解决争端并无异议，仅对快速仲裁是否可以通过临时仲裁解决发生争议。快速仲裁相对于普通仲裁而言，更加高效、便捷、经济，其核心在于简化了仲裁程序、缩短了仲裁时间、降低了仲裁费用等，从而使当事人的争议以较为高效和经济的方式得到解决。而临时仲裁庭相对于常设的仲裁机构而言，也具有高效、便捷、经济的特点。具体到本案，双方同意通过快速仲裁的方式解决争议，但该快速仲裁并未排除通过临时仲裁的方式解决，当事人在仲裁听证过程中也没有对临时仲裁提出异议，在此情形下，由临时仲裁庭作出裁决，符合双方当事人的合意。故应认定案涉争议通过临时仲裁庭处理，并不存在与仲裁协议不符的情形。

（生效裁判审判人员：姜欣、蔡晓文、吴勇）

指导性案例201号

德拉甘·可可托维奇诉上海恩渥餐饮管理有限公司、吕恩劳务合同纠纷案

（最高人民法院审判委员会讨论通过 2022年12月27日发布）

关键词 民事/劳务合同/《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》/国际单项体育组织/仲裁协议效力

裁判要点

1.国际单项体育组织内部纠纷解决机构作出的纠纷处理决定不属于《承认及执行外国仲裁裁决公约》项下的外国仲裁裁决。

2. Where the parties agree that disputes shall be submitted to an international individual sports organization for resolution, and if the international individual sports organization has no jurisdiction, then the dispute shall be submitted to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) for arbitration, and there are no circumstances of invalidity as provided by the applicable law, such agreement shall be deemed valid. If the international individual sports organization actually exercises jurisdiction over the dispute, and the dispute in question does not meet the conditions under which the parties agreed to initiate arbitration, the People's Court shall have judicial jurisdiction over the dispute in accordance with law.

Relevant Laws

1. Article 18 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations of the PRC

2. Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 1 of the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards

Basic Facts

On January 23, 2017, Shanghai JuYundong Football Club Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Juyundong Company) entered into a Professional Coach Employment Contract with the plaintiff, Serbian coach Dragan Kokotovic, stipulating that Dragan Kokotovic would serve as a professional coach to provide coaching services to the football club under Juyundong Company. On July 1, 2017, the parties entered into a Termination Agreement, which stipulated that the Professional Coach Employment Contract would terminate as of that date, and Juyundong Company would pay Dragan Kokotovic the remaining wages and other amounts. Regarding dispute resolution, Article 5.1 of the Termination Agreement provided that "any disputes or legal actions related to or arising from this Termination Agreement shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the FIFA Players' Status Committee or any other competent FIFA body." Article 5.2 provided that "if FIFA does not have jurisdiction over any dispute, the parties shall submit the aforesaid dispute to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) for arbitration in accordance with the Rules of Arbitration Related to Sports. The relevant arbitration proceedings shall be held in Lausanne, Switzerland."

Because Juyundong Company failed to pay the corresponding amounts in accordance with the agreement, Dragan Kokotovic applied to the Players' Status Committee for resolution of the dispute in question. On June 5, 2018, the Players' Status Committee issued a Single Judge Decision, requiring Juyundong Company to pay Dragan Kokotovic the remaining wages and other amounts within 30 days from the date of receipt of the notice of the decision. The Single Judge Decision also stated that if a party objected to the decision, it should appeal to the CAS in accordance with the prescribed procedures; otherwise, the Single Judge Decision would become a final and binding decision. Subsequently, neither party appealed the Single Judge Decision to the CAS.

Afterwards, Juyundong Company changed its name to Shanghai Enwo Catering Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Enwo Company), and Lyu En became its sole shareholder and legal representative. Because Enwo Company failed to make payments in accordance with the Single Judge Decision, and because the Juyundong Club had been dissolved and was no longer registered with the Chinese Football Association, the aforesaid decision could not be enforced through the autonomous mechanism of the football industry. Dragan Kokotovic filed a lawsuit with the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai, requesting the court to order: 1. Enwo Company to pay Dragan Kokotovic the remaining wages and other amounts; 2. Lyu En to bear joint and several liability for the aforesaid debts. During the period for submitting their defense, Enwo Company and Lyu En raised objections to the People's Court's acceptance of the case, arguing that, as stipulated in Article 5.2 of the Termination Agreement, the dispute in question should be submitted to the CAS for arbitration, and the People's Court had no jurisdiction, requesting a ruling that Dragan Kokotovic's lawsuit should not be accepted.

Judgment

The Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai rendered a civil ruling on January 21, 2020 [(2020) Hu 0104 Min Chu No. 1814], dismissing Dragan Kokotovic's lawsuit. Dragan Kokotovic, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, filed an appeal. The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, after trial and reporting to the Shanghai High People's Court and the Supreme People's Court for review in accordance with Article 8 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Reporting and Review of Cases Involving Judicial Review of Arbitration, rendered a civil ruling on June 29, 2022 [(2020) Hu 01 Min Zhong No. 3346], ordering: 1. The civil ruling of the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai [(2020) Hu 0104 Min Chu No. 1814] is reversed; 2. The case is remanded to the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai for trial.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the issues in dispute in this case include two aspects: First, whether the Single Judge Decision made by the Players' Status Committee constitutes a foreign arbitral award under the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (the New York Convention); Second, whether the arbitration clause in question can exclude the jurisdiction of the People's Court.

First, the Single Judge Decision made by the Players' Status Committee in this case does not constitute a foreign arbitral award under the New York Convention. According to the purpose, object, and provisions of the New York Convention, an arbitral award under the New York Convention refers to a final and binding award made by a permanent arbitral body or an ad hoc arbitral tribunal on the basis of an arbitration agreement between the parties to resolve disputes submitted by the parties. The Single Judge Decision made by the Players' Status Committee does not meet this definition. The decision-making process of the FIFA Players' Status Committee is not an arbitration procedure but an internal procedure of industry self-regulation for dispute resolution. First, the Players' Status Committee is an internal autonomous dispute resolution body of an international individual sports organization that accepts and handles disputes in accordance with internal regulations and rules, not an independent arbitral institution. Second, the Players' Status Committee only mediates disputes between its member units and members, and the Single Judge Decision it renders is an internal decision of the international individual sports organization, which is mainly enforced through the internal autonomous mechanism of the industry and does not have universal and strict binding force; therefore, it does not conform to the essential characteristics of an arbitral award. Third, pursuant to Articles 22 and 23(4) of the FIFA Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players, FIFA's handling of relevant disputes does not affect the right of a player or club to seek relief from a court regarding the dispute, and a party may also appeal the decision of the Players' Status Committee to the CAS. The aforesaid provisions clarify that FIFA's decisions are not final and do not exclude the parties' right to seek judicial relief. In summary, the Single Judge Decision made by the Players' Status Committee does not meet the definition of an "arbitral award" under the New York Convention and should not be recognized as a foreign arbitral award.

Second, the arbitration clause in question cannot exclude the People's Court's jurisdiction over this case. The parties in this case stipulated in Article 5 of the Termination Agreement that disputes should first be submitted to the Players' Status Committee or other internal bodies of FIFA for resolution, and if FIFA has no jurisdiction, then to the CAS for arbitration. Since it has been clarified that the dispute resolution procedures of the Players' Status Committee and other internal bodies of FIFA are not arbitration procedures, the relevant agreement does not affect the People's Court's jurisdiction over this case. However, the parties' agreement to submit disputes to the CAS for arbitration is essentially an agreement concerning the arbitration authority, so it is necessary to further examine the validity of the arbitration agreement and whether it excludes the People's Court's jurisdiction.

Because the arbitration clause in the agreement in question did not explicitly stipulate the applicable law, in accordance with Article 18 of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations of the PRC, the law applicable to the validity of the arbitration clause in question should be Swiss law. During the review of the validity of the arbitration agreement in question by the Supreme People's Court in accordance with Article 8 of the Provisions on the Reporting and Review of Cases Involving Judicial Review of Arbitration, it was ascertained that the Swiss legal provision on the validity of arbitration agreements is Article 178 of the Swiss Federal Code on Private International Law. This article provides for the validity of arbitration agreements as follows: "(1) As to form, an arbitration agreement is valid if made in writing, by telegram, telex, facsimile, or by any other means of communication that can constitute a written proof. (2) As to substance, an arbitration agreement is valid if it conforms to the law chosen by the parties, or to the law governing the subject matter of the dispute, in particular the law applicable to the main contract, or to Swiss law. (3) The validity of an arbitration agreement cannot be contested on the ground that the main contract may be invalid or that the arbitration agreement relates to a dispute not yet arisen." Based on the analysis of the facts found, the provision in Article 5.2 of the Termination Agreement complies with the above Swiss legal provisions, so the arbitration clause is legal and valid. However, according to the terms of the arbitration clause, only when "FIFA does not have jurisdiction" can the dispute in question be submitted to the CAS for arbitration. Since the Players' Status Committee has already accepted the dispute in question and rendered the Single Judge Decision, FIFA has exercised jurisdiction over this dispute. Therefore, this case does not satisfy the conditions set forth in the arbitration clause for submitting the dispute to the CAS for arbitration. Consequently, the arbitration clause does not apply to this case and cannot exclude the jurisdiction of the first-instance court as the People's Court of the defendant's domicile.

(The judges of the effective judgment: Qiao Lin, Zhao Juan, Hou Xiaoyan)
